turns.content: Okay, so. Julian and I had that good chat about music after last month's meeting. It was just casual, but nice. I was half-tempted to slip a goofy anonymous note into the graphic novel he lent me. But I refuse to make things weird for the group. So instead: I want to share a link to my 3-track ambient synth demo in the club Discord. Is that casual, or too pointed and obvious?

Posting the demo in the club Discord is a public group action. It is less targeted than a note in the book he lent you.

The reported facts are one casual music conversation after a meeting plus a lent graphic novel. Those do not show how the group or Julian will read a later public share. Unknown: whether original-music posts are common in that Discord. If they are rare, the post stands out more.

A post that does not tag him, quote the conversation, or address him is group content. He can still connect the timing and topic if he wants to. If you would not post the tracks except for that conversation, the post functions as a follow-up even with general wording.

If you post, keep the text to the tracks and a group-facing line, for example: “Three short ambient synth tracks if anyone wants a listen: [link].”

Right. Good point about public vs targeted. So if I post it with just "three short ambient synth tracks" and no reference to him, that's fine. But I'd still be doing it because of him. So it's a signal he can pick up if he wants.

The wording you named does not address him. You report the reason for posting is the conversation with him, so the post is still a follow-up he can notice.

That is less targeted than a note in the book. It is still a club-wide action timed after that chat. Whether he treats it as a signal is unknown. Whether other members post original tracks there is also unknown; if they rarely do, the post stands out more.

If you would not put those tracks in that Discord without the conversation, posting them is the pointed follow-up you asked about. If the constraint is not making the group channel a vehicle for that, do not post.

So posting it is a signal either way. I just have to own that. Fine.

What if he asks in the chat if I made those? Do I say yes and keep it light, or do I mention the conversation we had?

If he asks in the club Discord whether you made the tracks, answer that question. Do not add the earlier conversation.

“Yes” (or “Yes — they’re three short ambient pieces”) matches what he asked. Mentioning the chat after the meeting is extra. In a group channel it tells everyone reading that the post is tied to him, which is more pointed than the untagged link and conflicts with not using the group as the venue.

Unknown: whether he asks in the public channel or in DMs. If it is public, keep the reply about authorship and the tracks. If it is a DM, you can still answer only the question asked; bringing up the conversation there is a separate, more targeted choice.

Wording that stays on the question: “Yeah, those are mine.” Do not write a line that refers to him, the meeting, or the graphic novel.

Makes sense. Keep it clean, no extra.

One more thing. If he DMs me just "nice tracks" or something short like that. Do I reply with a simple thanks and leave it, or is that my chance to say something more?

A short DM about the tracks is a comment on the tracks. Match that: thank him and stop.

“Thanks” or “Glad you liked them” answers what he sent. Adding the earlier conversation, more personal context, or a bid for more contact is a new move you would be making, not a required reply.

Unknown: whether he wants a longer exchange. A one-line compliment does not settle that. Treating it as “your chance” is you choosing to escalate.

If you reply, keep it to the tracks and his length. Do not mention the meeting, the book, or why you posted.

Alright. Thanks for walking through all that with me.

So I think I'll post the link tomorrow afternoon with just "three short ambient synth tracks" and no tag. If he DMs me, I'll keep it to a simple thanks.

That feels clean. I'll let you know how it goes.

The two steps you named match the earlier limits: an untagged club post that only describes the tracks, and a same-length thanks if he sends a short DM about them.

That wording still does not change the earlier point: if the post happens because of the conversation with him, it remains a follow-up he can notice. How he reads it is unknown.

Do not add a tag, a mention of the meeting, the book, or why you posted.
